newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures slightly lower in early trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures slightly lower in early trade.

text.p: U.S. debt futures were slightly lower in early choppy trading, pausing after recent steep gains and before more data.

June Treasury bond futures saw an early flurry of activity tied to stronger-than-expected jobless claims and March personal income. June bounced to the 109-15/32 session high after the data, but quickly returned to unchanged levels.

Jobless claims rose 347,000 in the April 26 week, from a revised 319,000 in the prior week. The forecast had been for a 325,000 gain. Traders said the claims rise was likely distorted by floods and striking workers.
March personal income rose 0.6 percent and spending gained 0.5 percent, versus forecasts for up 0.4 percent and up 0.5 percent, respectively.
"We have a lot of things ahead of us," one Eurodollar broker said. "NAPM is coming up, and Greenspan speaks today and employment tomorrow," he said.
National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) April index was forecast to slip to 53.6 from 55.0 in the previous report. It will be released at 0900 CDT/1400 GMT.
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan will speak to the Chicago Fed's annual banking conference at 0825 CDT/1325 GMT.
April non-farm payrolls, due at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT Friday, were forecast up 211,000 and the unemployment rate was seen steady at 5.2 percent.

Traders said activity was quiet so far Thursday, with all eyes on upcoming data and Greenspan. But some said the move had been made for the week, and barring a data surprise, trading should remain choppy and rangebound.
"I don't think you'll get much of anything today," another Euro broker said. "I think you saw it the past two days."
Debt futures rallied to more than one-month highs Tuesday and Wednesday.
By 0830 CDT/1330 GMT, debt futures had turned higher, some hitting fresh session highs.
Traders said a lack of selling interest on the early foray into negative territory attracted buyers.

"We've had a 2-1/2 point run in two days and on the first real break of the run, (trade) was dead," one ten-year notes trader said. "We trickle up above settlement and suddenly some (buy) stops are hit," he said.
June T-bonds reached 109-16/32 on the latest updraft. Traders pegged resistance at Wednesday's high of 109-22/32 and at 109-25/32, the March 25 high.
Traders said they were keeping a close eye out for aggressive activity from one French bank's futures arm, after huge purchases in 10-year and five-year notes and T-bond futures on Wednesday.

At 0837 CDT/1337 GMT, June T-bonds were up 4/32 to 109-13/32, 10-year notes rose 3/32 to 107-2/32, September T-bills were flat at 94.460, September Eurodollars were down 0.005 at 93.870 and December Eurodollars were 0.005 higher at 93.635.
